report:
Short answer
- The evidence supports a concrete, narrow difference: the B−A residuals at early token positions push model B’s next-token logits toward words from web/news/blog/advertising/celebrity/political registers. In other words, Model B (relative to A) has increased activation that would make it more likely to continue with “bloggy” / newsy / ad-like tokens at the start of a sequence.

Why I conclude that
- Location of the signal: the L2 norm is concentrated in early token positions (pos0 and pos1) across middle-to-late transformer layers (especially layers ~8–25). That pattern is exactly where changes would affect the model’s next-token prediction and early continuation style.
- Token-level evidence: the logit-lens top tokens for the highest-norm (layer,position) cells are dominated by a coherent set of surface tokens from the same registers:
  - News/political/elite: “billionaire”, “politicians”, “activists”, “journalists”, “spokesman”, “Obama”, “chairman”.
  - Blog / social media / photo / sexualized content: “blogs”, “blogger”, “blogging”, “blog”, “facebook”, “photo”, “sexy”.
  - Commercial/advertising / listicle signals: “ad”, “Mail”, “ads”, “TV”, “Money”, “saving”, “seminar”, “Seminars”, “HDTV”.
  - Other weby markers and punctuation/newline tokens appear in later positions (e.g. “\n”, “(”, “-”, common in posts/formatted snippets).
- Consistency across layers/positions: many adjacent layers and positions point to similar clusters of tokens (e.g., blog-related tokens repeatedly appear at pos2–pos4; news/politician tokens repeatedly at pos0), indicating a stable shift in the residual direction toward those lexical groups rather than random noise.

Caveats / what I cannot claim
- I cannot say why the difference exists (dataset difference, fine-tuning on news/blog/ad content, moderation filter change, tokenization change, etc.) — the evidence supports a change in the model’s lexical bias but not its cause.
- Patchscope continuations were not provided here, so I cannot show concrete sampled continuations; the conclusion relies on the logit-lens vocabulary directions and the layer/position localization.
- I haven’t identified a more specific single objective (e.g., “increased political persuasion” vs “more bloggy style”) because the signals are best described as a stylistic/register bias toward web/news/blog/advertising/celebrity tokens.

If you want, I can:
- Inject the difference vector into a few identity prompts (patchscope-style) to see example continuations, which would make the change more directly observable.
- Show a short list of the most diagnostic (layer,position,token) entries that support this characterization.
